newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: MARGIN SQUEEZE HITS DSM Q3 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: MARGIN SQUEEZE HITS DSM Q3 RESULTS.

text.p: Dutch petrochemicals group DSM NV reported lower than expected third quarter earnings on Tuesday, saying its results were hit by a margin squeeze.
Net profit fell to 178 million guilders ($104 million) from 234 million in the third quarter of 1995. Analysts had forecast net profit of 181 to 212 million guilders.
DSM said earnings were squeezed at both ends by lower prices and higher feedstock costs which led to narrower margins. Sales volumes had risen for almost all of its main products.
DSM said it expected the supply and demand situation for its main products to remain good during the coming months.
However, fourth quarter results would be affected by higher feedstock costs and by several planned maintenance shutdowns.
"We expect that it will only be possible to pass on a part of the increase in feedstock costs via the prices of our products," DSM said.
"All things considered, we maintain our previous forecast that 1996 will be a good year," it added.
Shares in DSM traded 4.90 guilders lower at 161.70 guilders on Tuesday after the chemicals group reported lower than expected third quarter earnings.
The shares initially sunk as low as 160.00 guilders to show a loss of 6.60 as DSM said third quarter net profit fell to 178 million guilders from 234 million because of a margin squeeze.
Analysts said they would probably reduce their full-year earnings estimates in the light of the third-quarter results.
"Net profits were only slightly lower than the 186 million guilders we were expecting, but the quality of earnings has deteriorated," said Bert Schouten, analyst with MeesPierson.
